sentences.text: Revenue moved from $41.9 billion in FY2016 to $47.9 billion in FY2025, a 1.5% CAGR [F1][F10][F219].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 13.5% in FY2017 and 5.3% in FY2018, then recovered 17.1% in FY2021 [D42][D93][D246].
The FY2017 decline reflected refranchising of bottling operations, which cut operating cash flow by 20% that year [P75].
Operating income jumped 37.7% in FY2025 to $13.8 billion, driven by lower other operating charges after the prior-year fairlife remeasurement [D450][F40][P12].
Concentrate operations supplied 59.4% of FY2025 revenue and 1.6pp of its 1.9% growth [D532][D534][D449].
US finished product operations added 1.3pp of growth on a 21.2% revenue share [D562][D560].
Worldwide concentrate sales volume grew 1% in FY2025 with unit case volume even [P16].
Operating income grew 37.7% against 1.9% revenue growth, so incremental operating margin reached 428.4% [D450][D449][D473].
Diluted EPS rose 23.6% against 23.3% net income growth, with the diluted share count down 0.2% [D453][D451][D468].
Operating margin of 28.7% in FY2025 sits above the 26.0% window median and is the window high [F50][D766][D765].
Gross margin rose 0.6pp to 61.6%, against a 60.7% window median [F30][D462][D772].
The 7.5pp operating-margin gain came mostly from a 6.2pp residual swing in other lines, tied to lower other operating charges [D463][D477][P12].
Cost of revenue added 0.6pp and SG&A 0.7pp, the latter on lower foundation contributions and incentive expense [D475][D476][P13].
Net margin of 27.3% trailed operating margin by 1.4pp, with a 17.9% effective tax rate [F70][D810][D435].
Operating cash flow of $7.4 billion was only 0.57x net income, the window low against a 1.18x median [F100][D436][D799][D800].
Free cash flow of $5.3 billion was 0.40x net income and an 11.0% margin, versus a 20.2% median [F120][D437][D433][D775].
FY2024 operating cash flow fell 41% on a $6.0 billion IRS tax litigation deposit [D404][P22].
Capex of $2.1 billion was 4.4% of revenue and 2.01x D&A [F110][D432][D438].
Cash and investments were $10.3 billion at FY2025, and the current ratio reached a window-high 1.46x [D440][F200][D780].
Net debt was $32.4 billion in FY2023, but long-term debt is not reported after that year, so later net cash is not comparable [D341][X194].
Buybacks and dividends of $9.5 billion were 179.9% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D444][D445].
Return on average equity of 46.0% ranked at the 67th percentile against six staples peers, whose median was 36.5% [D448][D797][D798].
FY2017 and FY2018 revenue in the table are later recasts, $36.2 billion and $34.3 billion against $35.4 billion and $31.9 billion first reported [F2][X2][F3][X3][R1].
Long-term debt stops at FY2023, so total debt and net cash after that omit it [X194][R9].
Cash and investments omit an unmapped short-term investment line, understating the FY2025 total by $3.6 billion [F160][D440][R11].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [D344][D395][D445][R2].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2024 and FY2025 [D387][D437][R3].
If operating margin falls back below the 26.0% window median, the FY2025 charge-driven gain would look temporary [D766].
Operating cash flow at or above the 1.18x net income median would reverse the FY2025 conversion low [D800][D799].
Buybacks and dividends falling back toward the 94.8% of free cash flow seen in FY2022 would ease the FY2025 179.9% payout [D293][D445].

failures.sentence: Buybacks and dividends back under 100% of free cash flow would ease the FY2025 179.9% payout [D445].
